The "open-door notes" were two 1899–1900 diplomatic notes from U.S. Secretary of State John Hay to the major powers, asking them to respect equal trade access in China and its territorial integrity. The team note is wrong to call them a statement about Chinese immigrants: they concerned trade, not immigration, and Chinese immigration to the U.S. was in fact restricted by the Chinese Exclusion Act of 1882. My earlier "I don't know" was also wrong, since this is well-documented history that didn't need a file search.

CONFIDENCE: 90
